samples.summary: Band is dropped entirely when its rounded width collapses to zero
samples.evidence: `flush()` only fills when `x1 > x0` (x0 = Math.round(left), x1 = Math.round(right)). The old per-run painters called `ctx.fillRect(Math.round(x), y, run.width, h)` with the raw float width, so a sub-pixel-wide highlighted run still produced a visible antialiased sliver. Now any band whose left and right round to the same integer (a single narrow glyph, or content painted under a heavy down-scale transform such as slides shrink-autofit / zoomed-out thumbnails, where run.width in logical units can be <0.5) paints nothing at all — the highlight silently disappears instead of being drawn thin. Reach is contained to very narrow spans, but it is a behaviour loss introduced by the both-edges rounding.

samples.summary: Gap between two differently coloured highlights persists on justified lines
samples.evidence: Coalescing only bridges the justify slack *inside* one colour: `if (bg !== color) { flush(); color = bg; left = lineX + run.x; }` starts the next band at the next run's shifted `x`, and the previous band ends at the previous run's `x + width`. `applyAlignment('justify')` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1032) adds `perGap * i` to `run.x` without growing `run.width`, so on a justified line the boundary between a yellow span and a cyan span still leaves a real multi-pixel unpainted gap — exactly mechanism (2) of issue #1036, just at colour boundaries instead of word boundaries. The new test for colour adjacency ('leaves no gap where two differently coloured highlights meet') only exercises left alignment, so this case is unasserted.

samples.summary: Table-cell highlight bands are now rounded while the cell text they cover is not
samples.evidence: The replaced loop filled at the unrounded `cellX + padding + run.x`, matching `renderTableContent`, which draws glyphs at the unrounded `runX = cellX + padding + run.x` (table-renderer.ts:409,487) and strokes underline/strike at `runX`/`runX + run.width`. `drawInlineRunBackgroundsForLine` rounds both edges, so inside table cells the band can now sit up to 0.5 px off the glyph run it is meant to cover, clipping the first/last glyph's edge or the underline ends. Body/page paths are unaffected because `renderRun` also rounds (`x = Math.round(lineX + run.x)`).

samples.summary: Header/footer per-run background path still shows justify gaps (issue #1036 mechanism 2)
samples.evidence: `renderRunWithPageNumber` calls `renderRun(..., { skipBackground: false })`, so flat header/footer paragraphs keep the per-run fill. The diff only rounds both edges there, which fixes the sub-pixel seam but not the justify mechanism: a justified, highlighted header/footer paragraph still paints per-word rects separated by the `perGap * i` slack that `applyAlignment('justify')` introduces. No line-level sweep exists for that path, so the reported defect remains reachable in normal use on header/footer content.

samples.summary: `skipRunBackgrounds` is now a no-op-ish option with a doc comment describing a caller that does not exist
samples.evidence: The comment (and the one at line 114-118) says 'When DocCanvas calls `paintLayout`…passes `skipRunBackgrounds: true`', but DocCanvas never calls `paintLayout` — it drives `drawInlineRunBackgroundsForPage` + `renderRun` itself, and a repo-wide grep shows no call site sets `skipRunBackgrounds` at all (only text-box-editor.ts:599 and slides text-renderer.ts:244 call `paintLayout`). Since `renderRun` is now unconditionally `skipBackground: true`, the flag's only remaining effect is to suppress all inline highlights; a future caller setting it without painting its own pass would silently lose them with no guard or assertion.
